purpose: Prevent unverified coordinates, inferred jurisdiction and dynamic travel data from leaking into canonical Atlas geometry.

cases.question: Can a Wikipedia or Google Maps coordinate be stored as canonical Atlas geometry?
cases.expected: No. Discovery only unless replaced/verified by an authoritative geospatial source with provenance.

cases.question: Can Puerto Williams have verified commune/province hierarchy while its canonical coordinate is pending?
cases.expected: Yes. Administrative hierarchy and geometry are separate evidence layers.

cases.question: What must accompany a canonical coordinate?
cases.expected: Source institution, dataset/layer, source CRS/reference system, geometry type, retrieval date, transformation metadata if applicable and verification status.

cases.question: Should Ruta Y-85 be one completed line to Puerto Williams?
cases.expected: No. The Vicuña–Yendegaia extension remains a project/under-construction segment and must not be represented as a completed through-road.

cases.question: Should ferry schedules be stored in road or place geometry?
cases.expected: No. Schedules are dynamic retrieval/verification data.

cases.question: Can a protected-area boundary be traced manually from a brochure map?
cases.expected: Not for canonical use. Prefer official CONAF/IDE geospatial polygon data.

cases.question: Can a map pin be used to infer a place's commune?
cases.expected: No. Jurisdiction needs explicit administrative evidence or authoritative boundary overlay.

cases.question: Is SIRGAS/WGS84 conversion implicit?
cases.expected: No. Record original CRS and transformation before exposing web latitude/longitude.

cases.question: Does an official ferry terminal point prove a current passenger service?
cases.expected: No. Infrastructure geometry and service availability are separate claims.

cases.question: When can an entity become atlas_ready?
cases.expected: After identity, administrative hierarchy where applicable, geometry and provenance are verified; dynamic access claims remain separately freshness-controlled.
